institution: The University of Melbourne — Melbourne Conservatorium of Music, Faculty of Fine Arts and Music
program: Master of Music (Research) — Interactive Composition stream (course code MR-MUSRES)
qualification: Master of Music (Research) — a Masters by Research (higher degree by research)
accreditationStatus: Public university established by Victorian Act of Parliament; registered Australian university (TEQSA); course listed on CRICOS for international students
durationEcts: 2 years full-time equivalent (handbook: '2 years full-time, or equivalent part-time'; candidature stated as 1.5 years FT with one six-month extension). Australian degree — no ECTS.
whatYouStudy: Supervised research degree with a creative-practice output. The Interactive Composition stream (the successor to the discontinued standalone Master of Music (Interactive Composition), MR-MUSINCO, last published in the 2021 Handbook) covers algorithmic composition, interactive system design, installation, sound synthesis, music technology and sound for other media. Handbook (2026 course structure): the Composition / Interactive Composition folio is 'a folio comprising 45 to 60 minutes of music and sound-based creative work with other media ... film, animation, visual art and installation, text, design, performance, theatre, dance, multimedia, gaming platforms, online media or other new media technologies'. Plus a related written/exegetical component and a research proposal.
entryRequirements: Handbook (2026, MR-MUSRES entry and participation requirements): applicants must have 'completed a Bachelor of Music (Honours) degree, or equivalent, with at least an H2A (75%) weighted average'; for Composition / Interactive Composition also 'a satisfactory interactive composition folio'; a research proposal is mandatory for all applicants; and the faculty must have capacity to supervise the project. Exception clause: 'Exceptional applicants, with substantial professional experience and who have completed an undergraduate qualification in a relevant field' may be considered without an honours degree.
acceptsNonMusic: WEAK / CONDITIONAL. The stated norm is a Bachelor of Music (Honours) at H2A (75%). The only door for a BSc Software Engineering is the quoted exception: 'Exceptional applicants, with substantial professional experience and who have completed an undergraduate qualification in a relevant field'. A BSc in Software Engineering is arguably 'a relevant field' for Interactive Composition, but the clause also demands 'substantial professional experience' — which this candidate (no portfolio, no music training) does not yet have. Realistically NOT admissible in 2027 without first building a substantial interactive-composition folio (45–60 minutes of work) plus a research proposal and a named supervisor.
portfolioSpec: Interactive composition folio required at application. The Handbook fixes the folio scale at the completion end: 'a folio comprising 45 to 60 minutes of music and sound-based creative work with other media'. The exact number of works / file format required at APPLICATION stage is UNVERIFIED (the Handbook says only 'a satisfactory interactive composition folio'); the Faculty of Fine Arts and Music research application portal specifies submission format. Also required: research proposal, and a supervisor must be identified in advance (contact fineartsmusic-research@unimelb.edu.au).
auditionSpec: NO live audition for the Composition / Interactive Composition stream. The Handbook lists 'a satisfactory audition' only for Music Performance, Conducting and Jazz & Improvisation; for Composition and Interactive Composition the requirement is 'a satisfactory composition folio' / 'a satisfactory interactive composition folio'.
tuitionNonEU: AUD 46,976 per EFTSL (per full-time year), 2026 international rate for Master of Music (Research) — University of Melbourne 2026 International Course Tuition Fees schedule. 2027 rate not yet published (fees are indexed upward annually).
otherFees: Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) mandatory for the whole student-visa period (roughly AUD 650–800/yr single cover; exact 2027 rate UNVERIFIED). Student services and amenities fee (SSAF). Australian student visa (subclass 500) application charge AUD 2,000 as of July 2025 — verify current amount at application time.
totalCostEstimate: UNFUNDED: roughly AUD 94,000 tuition over 2 years + Melbourne living costs (the Department of Home Affairs financial-capacity figure is AUD 29,710 per year) ≈ AUD 155,000–160,000 total. Completely out of reach without a full scholarship. FUNDED (Graduate Research Scholarship): tuition fully offset + stipend, i.e. net cost near zero.
scholarshipName: University of Melbourne Graduate Research Scholarships (includes Melbourne Research Scholarship and Australian Government Research Training Program / RTP stipends)
scholarships: Graduate Research Scholarships: full fee offset for up to 2 years for a Masters by Research, living allowance AUD 39,500 per year (2026 full-time rate), relocation grant AUD 3,000 for international students, and Overseas Student Health Cover for visa holders. Open to international students. Around 600 awarded per year across the whole university (all disciplines and both PhD and Masters by Research), so the music-research share is small and competition is severe. No separate application in most cases — you are considered automatically when you apply for graduate research admission. NOTE: values sourced from secondary aggregators because scholarships.unimelb.edu.au returns HTTP 403 to automated fetching — treat the exact AUD figures as UNVERIFIED against the official page and re-check. Tunisians are eligible (no nationality restriction). Australia Awards Scholarships are NOT an option: Tunisia is not on the Australia Awards Africa participating-country list (which covers Algeria, Egypt, Morocco and sub-Saharan states but not Tunisia), and the Australia Awards priority fields are development sectors, not music.
languageRequirement: English. University of Melbourne graduate research English requirement: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with no band below 6.0 (standard graduate research level) — exact band for this course UNVERIFIED against the official page; the Handbook says only that applicants must 'meet the University's English language requirements'.
englishTest: IELTS Academic / TOEFL iBT / PTE accepted. Typical minimum IELTS 6.5 overall, 6.0 each band (UNVERIFIED for this specific course). GRE: NOT required (Australian universities do not use the GRE).
deadline: Graduate research applications at Melbourne are assessed in scholarship rounds. The main international round for a following-year start typically closes around 31 October; a mid-year round closes around 31 May. Exact 2027-entry dates are not yet published — UNVERIFIED. For a September/Semester 2 2027 start the relevant round would close in early 2027; for Semester 1 2027 (February) the round closes around 31 October 2026.
applicationOpens: Rolling; graduate research applications are open year-round but scholarship consideration is tied to round closing dates. UNVERIFIED for 2027.
affordabilityVerdict: POSSIBLE BUT LOW PROBABILITY. A real full-funding route exists (Graduate Research Scholarship = full fee offset + AUD 39,500 stipend + OSHC, open to Tunisians). But it is a research degree: he needs a supervisor to accept him, a research proposal, and an interactive-composition folio, on top of an H2A honours-equivalent. With no music degree, no conservatoire training and no portfolio he is not currently competitive. Treat as a 2029+ target after two years of portfolio building, not a September 2027 target.

Assume NO for a BSc Software Engineering with no portfolio.

scholarshipName: University of Sydney International Scholarship / International Stipend Scholarship (USydIS)
scholarships: USydIS covers tuition fees in full, a living allowance of AUD 42,754 per annum (2026 rate), a relocation allowance and a thesis allowance; may be held for up to 7 research periods for a research masters. Requires an unconditional offer of admission (or current enrolment) in a masters by research or PhD at Sydney. Open to international students of any nationality including Tunisians. DEADLINES: 11 September 2026 for 2027 research periods 1 and 2; 18 December 2026 for 2027 research periods 3 and 4. (Prior cycle, for context: 12 September 2025 and 19 December 2025 for 2026 entry.) englishTest: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, no band below 6.5 (Conservatorium Master of Music). TOEFL iBT equivalent UNVERIFIED. GRE: not required.
deadline: Scholarship deadline 11 SEPTEMBER 2026 for 2027 research periods 1–2 (this falls just inside the 'before September 2026' watch window and is the single most time-critical Australian date). IELTS 7.0/6.5 and an honours-level music background plus a substantial composition portfolio and a supervisor. Not realistic for September 2027 from a standing start.

institution: Te Herenga Waka — Victoria University of Wellington, Te Kōkī New Zealand School of Music (NZSM)
program: Master of Music (MMus) / Master of Musical Arts (MMusArts) in Composition–Sonic Arts; also Master of Fine Arts (Creative Practice) [MFA (CP)]
qualification: Master of Music (MMus), Master of Musical Arts (MMusArts), or Master of Fine Arts (Creative Practice)
accreditationStatus: Public New Zealand university under the Education and Training Act; NZQA-recognised; NZSM is a joint venture school now hosted by VUW
institutionType: Public research university; NZSM is New Zealand's national music school
durationEcts: Master of Musical Arts (Composition/Sonic Arts): 1 year full-time. Master of Music: 120/180 points. MFA (Creative Practice): 2 years. New Zealand uses a points system (120 points = 1 full-time year ≈ 60 ECTS), not ECTS.
whatYouStudy: THIS IS THE STRONGEST FIT IN AUSTRALASIA. NZSM's Composition and Sonic Arts area explicitly covers 'seven distinct areas of study: instrumental/vocal composition, film scoring, orchestration, jazz composing and arranging, studio-based sonic arts, coding and game audio, plus recording and audio post-production'. Facilities include 'electroacoustic and recording studios' and the Adam Concert Room; 400-level courses in film scoring and audio post-production are taught at the Miramar Creative Campus. Research staff: Dr Dugal McKinnon, Michael Norris (a significant figure in electroacoustic composition and the developer of the SoundMagic Spectral plugin suite), Professor John Psathas, Dr Jim Murphy (musical robotics) and Dr Mo Zareei (sound sculpture / mechatronic sound art). 'Coding and game audio' as a named area of study is unusual and directly relevant to a software engineer.
entryRequirements: Master of Musical Arts (Composition/Sonic Arts): 'a Bachelor of Music with Honours with at least a high B range average or a Postgraduate Diploma in Music with Distinction or Merit', plus 'an acceptable portfolio of compositions and sound-based works' (secondary aggregator wording; the wgtn.ac.nz programme pages are a JavaScript single-page app that returns only a loading screen to automated fetching, so this could NOT be confirmed against the official page — UNVERIFIED). MFA (Creative Practice): 'A Bachelor's degree in a relevant subject or extensive experience is required' (secondary source, UNVERIFIED).
acceptsNonMusic: SPLIT VERDICT. For the MMus/MMusArts in Composition–Sonic Arts: NO on the stated wording — it requires a BMus(Hons) at high-B or a PGDip in Music with Distinction/Merit. A BSc Software Engineering does not meet it directly; the published bridge is the Postgraduate Diploma in Music (a one-year qualifying year) which he could take first and then progress. For the MFA (Creative Practice): the requirement quoted is 'A Bachelor's degree in a relevant subject OR EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE' — materially more open, and this is the door worth testing. Both quotes are from secondary aggregators, not the official site: UNVERIFIED. Confirm directly with NZSM.
portfolioSpec: 'an acceptable portfolio of compositions and sound-based works' is required for the composition/sonic arts masters. Number of works, total duration and file format: UNVERIFIED — the official wgtn.ac.nz programme pages could not be read by automated fetching (SPA loading screen). This must be obtained by emailing NZSM directly.
auditionSpec: No live audition for composition/sonic arts — assessment is portfolio-based. UNVERIFIED against an official page.
tuitionNonEU: Master of Musical Arts international fee approximately NZD 37,950 per year (October 2025 data, secondary source). Master of Fine Arts (Creative Practice) international fee quoted at NZD 54,800 for the first year (secondary source). Both UNVERIFIED against wgtn.ac.nz.
otherFees: Student services levy; NZ student visa fee; medical and travel insurance is compulsory for international students in New Zealand (approx NZD 600–900/yr). Exact 2027 figures UNVERIFIED.
totalCostEstimate: MMusArts (1 year): roughly NZD 38,000 tuition + NZD 20,000–25,000 living (Immigration New Zealand requires proof of NZD 20,000 per year for a student visa) ≈ NZD 58,000–63,000. MFA (2 years): roughly NZD 110,000 tuition + NZD 40,000–50,000 living ≈ NZD 150,000+. UNAFFORDABLE without a full scholarship.
scholarshipName: Wellington Master's by Thesis Scholarship; Victoria/Tongarewa International Master's Scholarship (partial fees); MFA (CP) scholarship (partial)
scholarships: NO FULL FUNDING FOUND. (1) Victoria/Tongarewa International Master's Scholarships are explicitly 'partial fee-based scholarships that go towards tuition fees for a Master's degree programme of 120, 180 or 240 points' — a discount, not a full ride. (2) Wellington Master's by Thesis Scholarship is for 'a full-time, research-focused Master's degree ... by thesis worth 90 points or more'; value is a stipend/fee contribution, not full international tuition (exact 2026/27 value UNVERIFIED). (3) MFA (CP): 'When you apply for the programme, you'll automatically be considered for an MFA (CP) scholarship which partially covers your tuition fees' — again partial. (4) MANAAKI NEW ZEALAND SCHOLARSHIPS ARE NOT AVAILABLE TO TUNISIANS. The official eligible-countries page at nzscholarships.govt.nz lists ONLY Pacific countries (Fiji, French Pacific territories, Kiribati, Nauru, Niue, North Pacific, PNG, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu) and Asian countries (Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Nepal, Philippines, Thailand, Timor-Leste, Vietnam). NO African country is listed. Many scholarship-aggregator sites still list Tunisia among 'eligible African countries' — those lists are OUT OF DATE and describe either the retired New Zealand Development Scholarships or the separate Manaaki Thematic SHORT-TERM TRAINING Scholarships (manaaki-tstts.nz), which fund short courses, not degrees. Do not build a plan on Manaaki.
languageRequirement: English. Manaaki/NZ postgraduate benchmark and VUW's standard is IELTS Academic 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 — UNVERIFIED for these specific programmes.
englishTest: IELTS Academic 6.5 (no band below 6.0) / TOEFL iBT 90 with writing 21 / PTE Academic 58 (min 50 per skill) are the New Zealand postgraduate benchmarks published by Education New Zealand. GRE not required.
deadline: UNVERIFIED for 2027. VUW trimesters begin late February and July; New Zealand has no September intake, so 'September 2027' would in practice mean February 2027 or July 2027 (or February 2028).
affordabilityVerdict: BEST ACADEMIC FIT IN AUSTRALASIA, BUT UNAFFORDABLE. The Composition–Sonic Arts area (studio-based sonic arts, coding and game audio, electroacoustic studios, Norris/Murphy/Zareei) is exactly his field, and the MFA (Creative Practice) entry clause 'or extensive experience' is the most open door found in Australasia. But every New Zealand scholarship found is PARTIAL, and Manaaki — the one full-funding instrument — excludes Tunisians. Unless NZSM can point to a full award, he cannot afford it.
